decisions.reason: As a core door-hardware family that fits the firm's established architectural systems business, management would usually continue it into a third year unless internal sales and specification uptake now clearly fall below aspiration.

The mitred handle family remains close to the firm's design-led core, but after another year without clear standout evidence the chance of portfolio pruning rises modestly while still favoring retention.

Because the multifunctional lever directly supports the firm's accessibility and integrated-solution strategy, behavioral search is more likely to focus on improving commercialization than abandoning it.
This adjacent handle line is still likely to be tolerated within portfolio slack, though a second year of unremarkable results would make it somewhat more vulnerable than stronger-signaled launches.
Its dedicated positioning and prior German Design Award remain indicators of above-aspiration external validation, so management would have little reason to withdraw it.
A finish option is easier to rationalize away if demand is weak or complexity costs disappoint, but it still complements the firm's coordinated premium offering strongly enough to be kept for now.
